subject: Content safety operations, escalation SLAs & evidence — consolidated response

Subject: Content safety questionnaire — initial request

Karthik,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call this morning. Attached is the FinTrust RFP content-safety worksheet (redacted) — our security team wants a consolidated response that covers: misuse monitoring & telemetry, policy rule management, user reporting and escalation timelines, evidence for logging integrity, and retention/export formats.

Key deadlines: we need a consolidated packet and evidence bundle by end of business next Wednesday (2027-06-30). A few clarifying points the security team flagged up front:
- What telemetry fields are captured for each generation request (tokens, model variant, route, customer id, request/response hashes)?
- Do you support real-time alerts to customers and do SLAs cover mean time to first alert?
- Evidence: canonical artifacts preferred (audit logs, sample alert notifications, SOC2 summary).

I've copied the security reviewers; let us know if you need additional time.

Regards,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Park <amelia.park@fintrust.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 15:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Content safety questionnaire — telemetry & evidence details

Amelia / Karthik — following up with the technical evidence you requested. Below is a concise mapping to the FinTrust worksheet questions and where to find artifacts in the attached/linked packet.

1) Telemetry fields captured per request (we persist at request granularity):
   - request_id, customer_id (tenant), model_id, model_variant, route_key, input_token_count, output_token_count, prompt_truncated(boolean), timestamp_utc, compute_node_id, kv_cache_status, request_hash (SHA-256), response_hash (SHA-256).
   - We also record inference latency buckets (p50/p95/p99) and batching metadata for billing and anomaly detection.

2) Real-time alerts & SLAs:
   - Customers can opt-in to webhook alerting and/or syslog export.
   - Our internal misuse detector triggers alerts on scored policy violations (threshold + heuristic); mean time to first alert (internal) target is 3 minutes for high-severity categories, 15 minutes for medium.
   - Customer-facing SLA: we provide a push notification (webhook) within 15 minutes for high severity, with follow-up acknowledgement within 4 business hours. These terms can be formalized in the Security Addendum (DocuSign link below).

3) Escalation workflow / human-in-the-loop
   - Automated triage -> enrichment (context + prior incidents) -> assign to on-call security analyst -> escalation to customer CS/SE for joint remediation.
   - Incident priority matrix and human-review sampling thresholds are included in escalation-playbook.md (attached).

4) Logging integrity & chain of custody
   - All telemetry and audit logs are write-once append-only in our logging pipeline (immutable S3 objects with object-lock). Logs are cryptographically checksummed; we store SHA-256 digests and provide exportable manifests.

5) Retention and export formats
   - Default retention: 90 days for high-durability hot logs, configurable up to 7 years for customers on Dedicated/Private deployments.
   - Export formats: NDJSON, CSV, and Parquet. We can provide signed, time-bound exports and a manifest with checksums.

6) Evidence artifacts included in packet (attached):
   - telemetry-matrix.csv (field-level mapping + sample rows)
   - escalation-playbook.md (triage & on-call workflow)
   - soc2-summary.pdf (scope & audit firm)

If you want, I can extract a 24-hour sample of telemetry for a synthetic tenant to demonstrate the fields. Let me know which export format you prefer.

Marissa Cole
Head of Security Operations — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: telemetry-matrix.csv, escalation-playbook.md, soc2-summary.pdf

From: Amelia Park <amelia.park@fintrust.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Content safety questionnaire — a few clarifications

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our reviewers:
- For the SLA you mentioned (webhook within 15 minutes for high severity), can you provide an historical example or sample alert with timestamps? We want to validate the end-to-end timing.
- For retention: for Dedicated customers, is retention enforced by policy or by customer configuration? Do you provide an admin UI/API to set retention windows?
- Chain of custody: are manifests signed by an HSM or a KMS key we can verify?

If you can include a tiny anonymized alert sample (one alert and the corresponding log objects with checksums) that would go a long way.

Best,
Amelia

On a side note: Friday's sync is OK for one of our engineers; we'll confirm attendees when you send the invite.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Park <amelia.park@fintrust.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Content safety questionnaire — export sample & implementation notes

Amelia — quick technical follow-up and an attachable sample.

- Historical alert sample: attached is a redacted sample_alert.json (one high-severity alert) plus two corresponding log objects (redacted) and their checksums. In the sample you can see the alert timestamp, event ingestion timestamp, and the webhook delivery attempt timestamps.
- Retention controls: for Dedicated and Private customers retention windows are configured per-tenant via the Admin API and enforced by policy at the storage layer (object-lock + lifecycle rules). The Admin UI also exposes retention controls; screenshots included in the FT-safety-evidence-packet.zip.
- KMS/HSM signing: manifests are signed using our KMS-backed signing key; for Private deployments we can configure a customer-supplied HSM (bring-your-own-key). Verification instructions are in the packet.

Next steps: I'll add the sample files to the packet and prepare the short export in NDJSON with manifest and checksums. We can also produce a 24-hour synthetic telemetry extract if you prefer.

Ben Carter
Senior Product Manager — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: sample_alert.json (redacted), sample_log_object_1.ndjson (redacted), sample_log_object_2.ndjson (redacted)
